caption: The American rail network at its real construction dates: 402,000 km laid between 1830 and 1916, the peak. Then watch it go pale — 59 % of what was ever built no longer carries a train. One caveat, stated plainly: the build-up is dated line by line, the abandonments are not. Individual closure dates are unknown, so everything that has since disappeared fades at once rather than year by year. Sources: Atack railroads GIS (Vanderbilt) for the construction, OpenHistoricalMap for what still runs.
